questions.question_text: What is one effective way to narrow down Google search results for a school project, as described in the chapter?

options.text: Use broad terms like “history” to get more results
Put exact phrases in quotation marks (e.g., “Civil War causes”)
Only click on the first result for quick answers
Avoid using filters to see all possible websitesCorrect Answer: B) Put exact phrases in quotation marks (e.g., “Civil War causes”)

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a common sign of fake news or an unreliable website according to the chapter?

options.text: A professional layout with no ads
A sensational headline with extreme claims in all caps
A clear author name and publication date
Links to primary sources like government reportsCorrect Answer: B) A sensational headline with extreme claims in all caps

questions.question_text: Which free academic resource mentioned in the chapter is best for finding classic literature or historical texts as eBooks?

options.text: Google Scholar
Khan Academy
Project Gutenberg
Citation MachineCorrect Answer: C) Project Gutenberg

questions.question_text: What is a key step to avoid plagiarism when taking notes for a research project, based on the chapter’s advice?

options.text: Copy text directly without marking it as a quote
Write down the author, title, and URL for every source you might use
Only cite sources if they are books, not websites
Use the same notes for multiple projects without updating themCorrect Answer: B) Write down the author, title, and URL for every source you might use

questions.question_text: How can citation tools likeEasyBibor Citation Machine help high school students with essays, as explained in the chapter?

options.text: They automatically write the essay content for you
They generate formatted citations and bibliographies in styles like MLA or APA
They check for fake news in your sources
They provide free access to premium academic journalsCorrect Answer: B) They generate formatted citations and bibliographies in styles like MLA or APA

questions.question_text: What should you do if you’re unsure about the credibility of an article found online for a school project, according to the chapter?

options.text: Use it anyway if it supports your argument
Cross-check the information with trusted sources like BBC or .edu websites
Ignore it and only use social media posts for research
Assume it’s true if it has a professional-looking designCorrect Answer: B) Cross-check the information with trusted sources like BBC or .edu websites
